note: grep confirms zero definitions of the old name remain; pycc_hir::exception::shadowed_builtin_exception_name is the current name and returns Option<String>, not bool. The referencing file is untouched by the diff, so the rename never reached it.

summary: poisonable_names returned an ImportFrom's source-side name instead of the name it binds locally, so an aliased project import both double-reported its own cascade and suppressed a genuine unrelated diagnostic
note: Reproduced both directions against the pre-fix binary before fixing, not accepted on the reviewer's word. `from .dep import helper as h` with a later use of `h` emitted the real C0001 plus a spurious unknown-class cascade on `h`; the same import with a later use of `helper` emitted only the C0001 and wrongly swallowed the genuine unknown-class diagnostic. Both flip after the fix, re-verified on the built binary.

summary: The Project imports section did not state that discovery falls back to the package walk when [project].entry cannot be canonicalized or is not an ancestor of the checked file
note: The behaviour itself was already implemented and tested in src/modules.rs; only the specification sentence was missing, so a reader would expect a diagnostic where none is emitted.

summary: poisonable_names had no Stmt::Import arm at all, so every rejected plain import statement poisoned nothing and double-reported alongside its own cascade
note: Same defect class as the round-2 finding but through a missing match arm rather than a wrong expression, and outside what the reviewer inspected -- found by asking which other sites dispatch on the same rule. Reproduced three ways against the pre-fix binary: `import pkg.dep as d` then `d`, `import pkg.dep` then `pkg`, and `import os` then `os` each emitted the real C0001 plus a spurious cascade. All three flip after the fix; `from . import dep` was already correct and stays a single diagnostic.

summary: poisonable_names' ImportFrom arm returned no names for any pycc_std-resolvable module, so a failing stdlib from-import (unresolved symbol, `as` alias, wildcard) double-reported: its own diagnostic plus every later cascade naming a name it would have bound.
note: Confirmed empirically in four shapes (C0002 + base cascade, C0002 + annotation cascade, `sqrt as s` + base, `*` + base). Pre-existing on main (origin/main's `poisonable_name` has no import arms at all), so not a regression of this diff -- but the diff's own `Stmt::Import` arm already switched to an exact does-it-lower criterion, and leaving the sibling arm on the old is-it-a-project-import criterion is exactly the affected-site-inventory omission issue-to-plan step 3 warns about. Fixed here rather than deferred: the arm now mirrors lower_import_stmt's stdlib success condition exactly, and a rejected wildcard poisons the module's export list via a new `pycc_std::module_symbol_names`.

summary: Claimed Loader::resolve's package_inits preload can invert load order so an import cycle reached indirectly through a subpackage module goes undetected.
note: Built the reviewer's own predicted-to-fail fixture: pkg/__init__.py does `from a import VALUE`, a.py does `from pkg import PKG`, entry imports pkg.sub.mod. `pycc check` reports error[E0108] `import cycle: pkg/__init__.py -> a.py -> pkg/__init__.py` at a.py:1:1, both via the indirect pkg.sub.mod entry and via a direct `import pkg`. The non-cycle variant (a.py importing pkg.sub.mod, closing no cycle) correctly exits 0 -- and its ordering matches CPython, which also runs pkg.sub.mod's top level before pkg/__init__.py completes.
